Title: Blended RAG: Improving RAG (Retriever-Augmented Generation) Accuracy with Semantic Search and Hybrid Query-Based Retrievers
Takeaway: The Cascaded Adaptive Blended RAG reduces query latency and neural vector search invocations by 40-60% while maintaining at least 95% of full static Blended RAG retrieval accuracy.
Authors: Sawarkar et al.
Abstract: This research proposes the Cascaded Adaptive Blended RAG, a lightweight pre-retrieval router that evaluates query specificity to reduce average query latency and neural vector search invocations by 40-60%, while preserving at least 95% of full static Blended RAG retrieval accuracy.

Title: Blended RAG: Improving RAG (Retriever-Augmented Generation) Accuracy with Semantic Search and Hybrid Query-Based Retrievers
Takeaway: The Cascaded Adaptive Blended RAG system reduces query latency and neural vector search invocations by 40-60% while maintaining at least 95% of full static Blended RAG retrieval accuracy.
Authors: Sawarkar et al.
Abstract: This research proposes the Cascaded Adaptive Blended RAG, a lightweight pre-retrieval router that evaluates query specificity to optimize retrieval efficiency. By implementing a fast BM25 pass for simple factual queries and escalating to full Blended RAG for complex queries, the system aims to reduce average query latency and neural vector search invocations by 40-60% while preserving at least 95% of full static Blended RAG retrieval accuracy.

Title: Blended RAG: Improving RAG (Retriever-Augmented Generation) Accuracy with Semantic Search and Hybrid Query-Based Retrievers
Takeaway: The 'Blended RAG' method improves RAG accuracy in Generative Q&A systems by combining semantic search techniques and hybrid query strategies, surpassing fine-tuning performance.
Authors: Kunal Sawarkar, Abhilasha Mangal, Shivam Raj Solanki
Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a prevalent approach to infuse a private knowledge base of documents with Large Language Models (LLM) to build Generative Q&A (Question-Answering) systems. However, RAG accuracy becomes increasingly challenging as the corpus of documents scales up, with Retrievers playing an outsized role in the overall RAG accuracy by extracting the most relevant document from the corpus to provide context to the LLM. In this paper, we propose the ’Blended RAG’ method of leveraging semantic search techniques, such as Dense Vector indexes and Sparse Encoder indexes, blended with hybrid query strategies. Our study achieves better retrieval results and sets new benchmarks for IR (Information Retrieval) datasets like NQ and TREC-COVID datasets. We further extend such a ’Blended Retriever’ to the RAG system to demonstrate far superior results on Generative Q&A datasets like SQUAD, even surpassing fine-tuning performance.

Title: Blended RAG: Improving RAG (Retriever-Augmented Generation) Accuracy with Semantic Search and Hybrid Query-Based Retrievers
Takeaway: Blended RAG, combining semantic search techniques and hybrid query strategies, improves retrieval accuracy in large-scale information retrieval datasets and Generative Q&A systems.
Authors: Kunal Sawarkar, Abhilasha Mangal, S. Solanki
Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a prevalent approach to infuse a private knowledge base of documents with Large Language Models (LLM) to build Generative Q&A (Question-Answering) systems.
